key_insight: RASP separates reading from writing: inference uses every LoRA atom, while training updates only a sparse subset within a single fixed-size adapter.
engineering_relevance: This design keeps adapter parameter storage constant across sequential vision tasks without reducing the available LoRA rank at inference.
method: A scene-modulated cosine router selects the top-q unlocked atoms for gradient updates while inference reads all atoms.
A Frobenius Gram coherence penalty separates active output directions from non-updated directions.
Router activation history and atom spectral norms determine a consolidation index for Cauchy step attenuation and boundary anchor locking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports matching or surpassing branch-expanding LoRA learners on CIFAR-100, CUB-200, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-A under a constant adapter parameter footprint, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Long-horizon learning may depend on how sparsity and anchor locking preserve enough unlocked capacity; the abstract does not quantify this trade-off.
paper_title: RASP: Read-All, Sparse-Plasticity Continual Learning in a Stationary-Size LoRA
